revision: 37e3522 baseline; treatment adds retained DATA plan refill
notes: Two normal release sweeps per build, each with four retained-daemon 20-second points: requested 16G, 21G, unlimited, 16G return. Same workload, binary identities and CPU placement; no builds or other tests overlapped measurement.

Baseline uses production ACK_BUFFERS=4 and default 4 MiB/s control budget. Treatment refills a retained never-attempted DATA plan before requesting another grant, using existing bounded frame/packet metadata and original payload storage.

Retained packet bytes and identities remain unchanged. Refill waits while a request/grant is outstanding and defers across packet-number gaps; partial/failed attempts, expiry, PMTU reduction and retirement still cancel discarded reservations.
No buffer-size, offload-window, control-rate, wire-format, receive-admission or congestion-control-policy changes.
Goodput excludes drain; missing ratios and drop deltas include drain. CPU 100% is one core; drop categories have different units and cannot be summed into exact lost frames.

Initial candidate runtime testing exposed a non-contiguous append after a canceled probe. A red regression reproduced 11–22 followed by 24 after canceled 23. The adjacency guard passed submission, ACK-to-zero-inflight, and fresh-plan checks; both full runtime tests then passed. Only the corrected frozen binary was benchmarked.

341 ordinary release tests,63 short kernel/integration tests, all-target/all-feature musl Clippy with -D warnings and formatting pass. The final combined tree also passes the full routed PMTU test; see final_validation.
First refill sweep has 13 reordered frames in L→R inner flow 52003 at 16G (0.0003124674%). All other points have zero reordering. No attribution is established.
All 16 points have zero malformed/invalid/duplicate/out-of-window/wrong-run records, admission pressure, outer socket overflow, inner UDP errors and outer IPv6 fragmentation.

Mean 21G goodput improves 23.90% / 26.95%; unlimited improves 17.70% / 49.48%. Individual directions remain variable: first refill sweep falls 18.13% forward from21G to unlimited; repeat rises 13.92%. These are not plateau or final performance-gate results.
ACK-buffer drops are a subset of queue_drops, not additive. Kernel SKB drops, expired frames and queue entries cannot be summed into exact frame loss.

final_validation.source: Refill plus the separate initial receive-registration ordering fix; the matched rate sweeps above precede that receive fix.
